result.topic_en: Variational calculation of an expression H involving curl-type differences of u and currents i, followed by Ohm's law for steady currents (div i = 0, grad λ = W i) and its derivation as the Euler-Lagrange equation of the integral of μ |∇λ|².
result.transcription:
$H = \cdot - \int\{\sum\left(\frac{\partial\Delta_h u}{\partial x_{h+1}}\,\delta u_{h-1} \mp \frac{\partial \Delta_h u}{\partial x_{h-1}}\,\delta u_{h+1}\right) \mp \sum i_h\,\delta u_h\}\,dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$
$+ \int\sum u_h\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x_h}\frac{\partial\delta u_k}{\partial x_k} - \frac{\partial^2\delta u_h}{\partial x_k^2}\right)dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$
$= \cdot - \int\{\sum\frac{\partial\Delta_{h+1}u}{\partial x_{h-1}}\,\delta u_h [-+-] - \sum\frac{\partial\Delta_{h-1}u}{\partial x_{h+1}}\,\delta u_h \mp \sum i_h\,\delta u_h\}\,dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$
$+ \int\sum_{h,k} [-u-]\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_h\partial x_k}\delta u_k - \frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_k^2}\delta u_h\right)dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$
$= \cdot - \int\sum\left\{\frac{\partial\Delta_{h+1}u}{\partial x_{h-1}} - \frac{\partial\Delta_{h-1}u}{\partial x_{h+1}} [-+-] - i_h\right\}\delta u_h\,dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$
$+ \int\sum_{h,k} [-u-]\left(\frac{\partial^2 u_k}{\partial x_h\partial x_k} - \frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_k^2}\right)\delta u_h\,dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$
$= \cdot\cdot - \int\sum_h\{\Delta_h\Delta u - i_h\}\,\delta u_h\,dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$
$+ \int\sum_h\left\{\frac{\partial}{\partial x_h}\left(\frac{\partial u_1}{\partial x_1} + \frac{\partial u_2}{\partial x_2} + \frac{\partial u_3}{\partial x_3}\right) - \left(\frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_1^2} + \frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_2^2} + \frac{\partial^2 u_h}{\partial x_3^2}\right)\right\}dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3\,\delta u$ 15

Ohm'sche Gesetz
$\frac{\partial i_1}{\partial x_1} + \frac{\partial i_2}{\partial x_2} + \frac{\partial i_3}{\partial x_3} = 0$
$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_1} = W.i_1$ $W$ = Widerstand, $\lambda$ nach Ohm d. electrische Spannung (für $\lambda$ = const kein Gleichgewicht weil d. h. die Electricitätsvertheilung[?] verschieden[?])
$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_2} = W.i_2$ $\lambda$ nach Kirchhoff das Potential der electrischen Kräfte (für diese Annahme entstehende Bewegung[?] parallel der Oberfläche[?])
$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_3} = W.i_3$
$\mu = \frac{1}{W}$ = Leitungsvermögen
also $\frac{\partial\,\mu\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_1}}{\partial x_1} + \frac{\partial\,\mu\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_2}}{\partial x_2} + \frac{\partial\,\mu\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_3}}{\partial x_3} = 0$
$\frac{\delta}{\delta\lambda}\int\mu\sum_h\left(\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_h}\right)^2 dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3 = H = 0$
$H\delta\lambda = \int 2\mu\sum_h\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_h}\cdot\frac{\partial\delta\lambda}{\partial x_h}\,dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3 = \int 2\mu\sum_h\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_h}\delta\lambda\,dx_{h-1}\,dx_{h+1} - \int 2\sum\frac{\partial\,\mu\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_h}}{\partial x_h}\cdot\delta\lambda\,dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$

methods.what: Integration by parts of the first variation of H, giving Euler-Lagrange terms (curl curl u minus current, plus grad div u minus Laplacian u)
Ohm's law for steady currents: divergence-free current
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial i_1}{\partial x_1} + \frac{\partial i_2}{\partial x_2} + \frac{\partial i_3}{\partial x_3} = 0$

methods.what: Ohm's law: gradient of potential equals resistance times current
Elliptic equation div(μ grad λ) = 0 for the potential
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial\,\mu\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_1}}{\partial x_1} + \frac{\partial\,\mu\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_2}}{\partial x_2} + \frac{\partial\,\mu\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial x_3}}{\partial x_3} = 0$

methods.what: Variational (Dirichlet-type) principle: the equation is the Euler-Lagrange equation of ∫ μ|∇λ|², via integration by parts into boundary and volume terms
